W.note: Counts 5-7-5 (sun gone from the street / a veil of ice up there still / burning pearl and rose); the street-to-sky cut is strong and nacreous clouds are evoked without being named, though 'veil' and 'pearl' are slightly familiar.

X.note: Counts 5-7-5 (Mother-of-pearl veils / nacreous light at dusk, slow / fire on frozen air); accurately names nacreous clouds and the ice-fire contrast, but mother-of-pearl is the stock phrase and the middle line is padded.

Y.note: Counts 5-7-5 (Winter dusk, sun gone / a veil too high for the dark / holds mother-of-pearl); the idea of a cloud too high for the darkness is accurate to polar stratospheric clouds and gives the poem its turn.

Z.note: Counts 4-7-5 (Nacreous glow = 4), so the opening line misses the form, and 'the sky holds its breath' is a stock closer.
